help.language:
The knobs, this panel, the dashboard cards and the notifications use this language.

“Automatic” follows Home Assistant's language. The language switch in the panel's header changes only your own browser; everyone else and the knobs keep this setting.
help.animation:
How much motion the knob's screen shows.

Full: every change, jump and celebration is animated, with confetti.

Reduced: every animation takes half as long, and there is no confetti. A good choice when the full animations feel slow or too much.

Off: nothing moves; the screen jumps from one state to the next. This is not smoother than the animated modes, only calmer; it can help a child who is distracted by motion.
help.inactivity: When nobody turns or presses the knob for this many minutes, it goes back to the child selector, so the next child starts on their own screen. Half a minute (0.5) works too.
help.routine_menu_grace:
After a routine ends it stays in the knob's menu while a child still has an open task in it, so the task can still be ticked.

When the last checkpoint also pays late (a band with negative minutes), the routine first stays as long as that pays, and this time starts after it.
help.background:
This background shows on every knob that has no background of its own. A knob's own background is set on the Knobs tab, in that knob's section.

After a change the physical knobs restart once, after a minute without use, to show the new picture. A virtual knob changes at once.
help.background_current:
The six backgrounds of the chosen theme: 1 to 3 are day scenes, 4 to 6 night scenes.

When you choose one of these, a theme change switches the background to the new theme's picture with the same number.
help.background_other: Any background of any other theme. It stays when the theme changes.
help.theme:
The theme is the look of the panel, the dashboard cards and the knobs: colours, fonts, icons, pictures and backgrounds. The children's avatars do not change with it.

After a change the physical knobs restart once, after a minute without use.
help.cards_themed:
On: the Kis Segítő dashboard cards take the theme's colours and fonts.

Off: they follow the dashboard's own theme, like the other cards. Their pictures come from the theme either way.
help.own_themes:
Here you can switch off themes you do not use (they leave the picker) and manage your own themes.

To make your own theme: download the template, replace any of its pictures with your own under the same file names, set the theme's name and colours in theme.json, zip it and upload it. Pictures you leave out stay the built-in ones. Uploading a theme with the same name again updates it. Full guide: docs/themes.md.
help.icons_own:
Own icons can be chosen everywhere an icon is chosen (tasks, checkpoints, routines, rewards) and show on the knobs too.

A switched-off icon is no longer offered, but whatever already uses it keeps it. The ⟳ button replaces its picture.
help.icons_builtin: Built-in icons cannot be deleted, only switched off: click an icon to switch it off or on. A switched-off icon is no longer offered, but whatever already uses it keeps it.
help.virtual: A virtual knob is the knob's screen as a dashboard card, without a device. Add it here, then add a “Kis Segítő” card to a dashboard and choose this knob in it.
help.knob_avatars: The avatars show the children who can use this knob. Without avatars, everyone can. Change the list in the knob's “Children on this knob” section.
help.knob_children: Ticked children can use this knob. A newly added child is ticked on every knob.
help.knob_hide_locked: On: the knob shows only the ticked children. Off: the others appear in the child selector too, greyed with a lock, and cannot be chosen.
help.knob_bg:
“Common” is the background chosen for every knob on the Look & theme tab. Here you can give this knob its own.

After a change the knob restarts once, after a minute without use, to show the new picture.
help.knob_bg_virtual: “Common” is the background chosen for every knob on the Look & theme tab. Here you can give this virtual knob its own; the card shows the new picture at once.
help.knob_new_key:
The knob downloads its pictures (avatars, photos, icons, backgrounds) from Home Assistant with its own secret key.

A new picture key makes the old one invalid at once, and the knob gets the new one automatically. Use it when the key may have got into the wrong hands, for example when the knob was given away or lost. In normal use it is never needed.
help.knob_restart: The knob restarts and can be used again after about half a minute. Useful when it does not react or does not show a new setting.
help.screen_own: Give this knob its own screen times. Empty fields use the general values of the Knob screen card.
help.sensors_inputs:
For a knob without sensors of its own, choose Home Assistant entities here: the knob gets their values as presence, distance or illuminance.

Left empty, the knob uses the sensors wired to it.
help.screen.saver_after: After this many minutes without use the knob starts its screensaver. 0 means never. Any turn or press wakes it.
help.screen.dim_after: After this many minutes without use the screen dims to the dimmed brightness. 0 means never.
help.screen.dim_level: The brightness of the dimmed screen, as a percentage of full brightness.
help.screen.blank_after: After this many minutes without use the screen goes black and the knob stops drawing, which saves energy. 0 means never.
help.screen.off_after: After this many minutes without use the backlight switches off too. 0 means never. Any turn or press wakes the knob.
help.screen.saver_type: What the screensaver shows: bouncing balls, confetti or stars.
help.sensors.title:
The sensor features work when the knob gets presence, distance or light values: from sensors wired to it, or from Home Assistant entities chosen at the knob (“Sensors from Home Assistant”).

The values here apply to every knob.
help.sensors.presence_wake: When someone comes near the knob, the screen wakes with a soft fade-in, without a press.
help.sensors.presence_saver: On: the screensaver time counts from when nobody is near the knob, not from the last turn. While someone stands there, the screen does not switch to the screensaver.
help.sensors.night_light: In the dark (below “Dark below”) the knob shows a warm white night light with a small moon to someone further away. Coming near brings up the child screen.
help.sensors.ambient: On: the screen brightness follows the room light between the minimum and the maximum brightness: dimmer in the dark, brighter in daylight.
help.sensors.near_cm: When someone is closer to the knob than this, the child screen comes up. Without a distance sensor, a turn or press brings it up.
help.sensors.night_lux: Below this many lux the room counts as dark, and the night light can come on.
help.sensors.night_brightness: The night light's brightness, as a percentage of full brightness.
help.sensors.night_kelvin: The night light's colour in kelvin. Lower is warmer and more yellow (2700 K is like a light bulb), higher is cooler and whiter.
help.sensors.night_off_after: The night light switches off this many minutes after nobody is near the knob any more.
help.sensors.ambient_min: The lowest brightness when it follows the room light, as a percentage of full brightness.
help.sensors.ambient_max: The highest brightness when it follows the room light, as a percentage of full brightness.
help.sensors.light_factor:
A light sensor behind the knob's window measures less light than the room has. For the night light and the brightness the knob multiplies the measured value by this number.

Measure the room with a light meter app and set the correction so that the room value shown below matches it. Details: docs/sensors.md.
help.streak:
A day counts for the streak when the child reached every checkpoint marked “Counts for the daily streak” on time that day. A day without such checkpoints does not change the streak; a missed or late one starts it again from zero.

Kis Segítő checks each day after midnight. When the streak reaches the set length, the child gets the streak reward and the streak starts again.
help.interest:
Once a week, on the chosen day and time, the piggy bank earns interest: the given percentage of the tokens in it, rounded down to whole tokens.

Only a child whose piggy bank is unlocked and has tokens in it gets interest.
help.interest_min: When set, the interest is at least this many tokens, even when the percentage would give less (for example for small amounts). Empty means no lower limit.
help.interest_max: When set, the interest is at most this many tokens, even when the percentage would give more. Empty means no upper limit.
help.export: Saves every setting, the children, routines, rewards, the whole token history, the event log and the approvals in one JSON file. Worth doing now and then, and before any bigger change or an import.
help.import:
Loads a file exported earlier, for example when moving to a new Home Assistant or after a mistake.

Importing replaces all current data with the file's content: children, routines, rewards, settings and the whole token history. This cannot be undone, so export first. The knobs' own keys and settings stay.
help.approvals:
Here you decide about the requests waiting for approval.

A reward's price is set aside until you decide and goes back to the wallet when you reject it.

A checkpoint's tokens are paid only when you approve it; when you reject it, the child gets no tokens for it, but its tasks stay done.
help.rewind:
Drag the slider back to an earlier time, and the cards, the ring and the progress bars show what had happened by then. This way you can see where the day stood in the morning or the afternoon.

“Back to now” returns to the present. The mouse wheel moves it a minute per notch, a quarter of an hour with Shift.
help.today_template: The day template says which routines run today. Here you choose another template for today only; the default for each weekday is set on the Calendar page.
help.modify_today: Changes here apply to today only; the routines themselves do not change. Every change is logged.
help.modify_row:
The − and + buttons move the routine's start and end by five minutes, for today only. “Skip today” takes the routine out for this day. “Restore” brings back the original times.

Click the routine's name to edit today's occurrence only.
help.one_day: A one-day routine runs on that single day and does not repeat. Everything else works as in a regular routine: tasks, checkpoints, rewards, and it shows on the knob.
help.day_only: These changes apply to this date only; the routine itself stays as it is. Parts marked ✎ differ from the routine. Every change is logged.
help.calendar_edit:
The calendar shows the routines as they run each day.

Click a routine to change it for that day only. Drag it to another time or another day; drag its top or bottom edge to change its start or end. This always changes only that occurrence. Click an empty spot to add a routine for that day only.

✎ marks an occurrence changed for its day, 1 a routine for one day only. Past days can only be viewed.
help.calendar_view: The calendar shows the routines as they run each day. ✎ marks an occurrence changed for its day, 1 a routine for one day only.
help.day_templates: A day template says which routines run on a day, for example Weekday, Weekend or Holiday. On days without a template every routine follows its own days.
help.weekday_templates: Choose the default day template for each day of the week. The template of a single date can be changed on the Today page.
help.template_routines: The ticked routines run on the days that use this template, whatever their own days are.
help.children_page: Each child's card shows their tokens, piggy bank and streak. Click a card to open the child's details and statistics; the arrows set the order on the knob.
help.child_stats: The statistics come from the token history and the task and checkpoint log: how much the child earned and spent, how punctual they were, and where they tend to slip. Choose the period at the top.
help.child_theme: On the knob, this child's screens use this theme. The child selector and the background keep the knob's common theme. The virtual knob and the single-child cards follow it too.
help.child_aliases: Other names the voice assistant (Assist) recognises for this child, such as nicknames. Separate them with commas. Optional.
help.child_color: The child's colour on the knob, the panel and the cards. When it is close to the colours of the knob's time ring (green, orange, red, gold), it can be harder to tell apart on the knob, so a warning is shown.
help.child_piggy: On: the child can use their piggy bank: put tokens in it, and it earns interest. When a reward of the “Unlocks the piggy bank” kind exists, the child can also buy the unlock.
help.child_active: A child switched off does not show on the knobs, on the Today page or in Assist, but all their data and history stay. You can switch them on again at any time.
help.routines_page: Set up the routines here: when they run, which tasks they have, and how many tokens finishing them on time brings. The knob shows the routine that is running.
help.rtemplates_page: Routines saved as templates can become a new routine with one click, or fill in the form of a new one.
help.rtemplate_use: Fills the form with a saved template: tasks, order, icons, timing, checkpoints and children. You can change anything afterwards.
help.rtemplate_save: Saves the routine under its own name as it is in the form (tasks, order, icons, timing, checkpoints, children). Later a new routine can be made from it, or a routine filled in with it.
help.routine_repeat: A repeating routine runs on the chosen days every week. A one-time routine runs only on the chosen date and does not repeat.
help.routine_days: The routine runs on these days every week. On a day with a day template, the template decides which routines run.
help.routine_children: With nobody ticked, the routine is for every child. With children ticked, it is only theirs.
help.routine_on_device: Off: the routine does not show on the knob, but it still counts on the panel, in the calendar and in the statistics. Useful for a routine only the parents follow.
help.routine_active: A routine switched off does not run anywhere: not on the knob, not in the calendar. Its settings stay, and you can switch it on again later.
help.routine_color: The routine's colour in the calendar views. The colours of the knob's time ring are set in the Time colours section.
help.zones: The colours of the arc on the knob's ring that shows time passing. The whole colour pattern shows from the routine's start; each colour zone starts this many minutes before the routine's end.
help.checkpoints:
A checkpoint is a timed goal within the routine, for example “Leave at 7:45”. It is reached when all its tasks are done; its reward depends on how early that is.

Checkpoints for everyone show on the knob's outer arc, checkpoints for single children on the inner arc.
help.cp_streak: On: this checkpoint counts for the daily streak: the day counts as a success only when the child reaches it on time.
help.cp_approval: On: the child does not get the checkpoint's reward at once. When it is reached, an approval request appears on the Today page: approving pays the tokens, rejecting does not. The tasks stay done either way.
help.cp_bands:
The reward bands say how many tokens the checkpoint brings, depending on how early it is reached. The best matching band counts.

Example: “15 minutes early → 5 tokens” and “0 minutes early → 2 tokens”. Finishing 20 minutes early brings 5 tokens, 5 minutes early brings 2. A negative value gives a late reward, for example “−10 → 1”: up to ten minutes late still brings 1 token.
help.task_checkpoint: Every task belongs to a checkpoint: the checkpoint is reached when all its tasks are done. “Last checkpoint” means the latest one, and it is the default.
help.rewards_page: The rewards appear in the knob's shop in this order. Hover a card to reorder. The child buys them on the knob with their tokens.
help.reward_photo: With an uploaded photo, the panel and – once the knob has downloaded it – the knob show the photo; otherwise the chosen icon.
help.reward_kind: A normal reward is a thing or an experience the child can buy with tokens. Buying the “Unlocks the piggy bank” reward gives the child their piggy bank: they can then put tokens in it, and it earns interest.
help.reward_confirm: On: when the child buys it, the price is set aside and a parent confirms or rejects the purchase on the Today page. On rejection the tokens go back to the wallet.
help.tokens_amount: A positive number adds tokens, a negative one takes them away. Every movement goes into the history, where it can be corrected or reversed.
help.tokens_account: The wallet holds the child's tokens to spend in the knob's shop. The piggy bank holds the saved tokens that earn interest every week; it can be chosen only when the piggy bank is unlocked.
help.history_events:
On: entries without token movements show too: tasks done and checkpoints without tokens. They are hidden by default, but search always finds them.

These entries can be corrected too: “Did not do it” puts one back to not done, and “Give tokens” credits the tokens afterwards when the child did it but forgot to press it in time.
help.history_corrections: “Change amount” changes an entry's effective amount, for example when a credit was mistyped. “Reverse” cancels an entry with an opposite one. Neither deletes anything: every step stays visible in the history.
help.notifications: Each rule sends a message about the chosen events and children to a Home Assistant notification target, such as the mobile app or a script. For your own automations every event is also available as kis_segito_event.
help.notify_label: Of the notification scripts, only those with this label appear as targets. Add the label to the scripts in Home Assistant: Settings → Automations & scenes → Scripts → Labels.
help.notify_target: Where the rule sends the message: a Home Assistant notify service (for example the mobile app on your phone) or a labelled script.
help.notify_fields: For a script, choose which of its fields gets the message text and which the title.
help.notify_fixed: Give the script's other fields a fixed value here, for example the recipient. They are the same in every message.
help.notify_events: The rule sends a message about these events. You can choose several.
help.notify_children: With nobody ticked, the rule is about every child's events. With children ticked, only about theirs.
help.notify_test: Sends a test message to the target with the current settings, so you can see whether it arrives.
